text:
oncall-alex: @channel :rotating_light: spike in inference request queue for customer-facing hosted API in us-west1. Autoscaler reports "max nodes reached" and pods are Pending due to no schedulable nodes. Visible throttling on /v1/generate endpoints. Paging SRE.

incident-bot: Incident created: GPU_POOL_SATURATION_US_WEST1 (sev=pg). PagerDuty alert routed to oncall-alex.

oncall-alex: Observed metrics: GPU utilization ~98%, pending pods ~42, queue length +1200 requests, p99 latency climbing from 180ms -> 2.3s. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/gpu/us-west1

sre-marc: copy. Are we hitting cloud quota or autoscaler maxNodes setting? Running `kubectl get hpa -n inference` shows HPA healthy but ClusterAutoscaler logs show "reached maximum node count".

devops-julie: Confirmed: autoscaling group for gpu-pool-us-west1 has desired=80, max=80. Looks like we hit the configured ceiling. Recent commit 1759 lowered max to 80 to control costs.

oncall-alex: That explains it. Can we temporarily raise max to 100? Need to assess risk/approval. Customer-impact: some paying customers seeing 5-20% error rate on batch/streaming calls.

customer-success-lee: We already have a handful of enterprise customers on Dedicated in us-west1 — they're pinging support. Notified major customers via status.

sre-marc: Immediate triage steps I propose: 1) increase autoscaler max to 100 (manual), 2) drain low-priority spot pools (evict non-critical jobs), 3) route new requests to secondary region (us-east1) with degraded performance fallback.

devops-julie: I'm iso for the next 15. I can bump the autoscaler but need an approval from infra or cloud-ops for temporary quota. @cloud-ops-tina can you approve manual cap raise and coordinate with cloud provider if we need a hard quota increase?

cloud-ops-tina: On it. I'll open a support case with the cloud provider and approve temporary increase for the autoscaling policy. ETA 18-30 mins for provider-side quota if needed.

oncall-alex: While that happens, let's clear pending backlog by scaling down noncritical workloads. Marc, can you run a targeted eviction for training jobs tagged "low-priority"?

sre-marc: Running:
```
kubectl get pods -n training -l priority=low -o name | xargs -r kubectl delete -n training
```

sre-marc: Deleted ~32 pods. That freed ~8 GPUs but still short.

devops-julie: I'm going to update the cluster autoscaler annotation to allow manual increase. Patch:
```
kubectl patch deployment cluster-autoscaler -n kube-system --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/args/3","value":"--max-nodes=100"}]'
```

devops-julie: Patch applied. Scaling policy now shows max=100. Requesting cloud provider scale up for additional nodes.

infra-bot: Autoscaler change detected by infra-bot. Audit log: user=devops-julie action=patch resource=cluster-autoscaler ts=1768001602

cloud-ops-tina: Cloud request submitted (case #CLOUD-98765). Provider acknowledged and queued for expedited quota bump. Estimated add time 12-25 mins.

oncall-alex: While nodes spin up, enable emergency routing to us-east1 for new generate requests. Patch API gateway route weight 85% us-west1 -> 15% us-east1.

devops-julie: Gateway rule updated. Command used:
```
redwoodctl route update --region us-west1 --failover us-east1 --weight 85
```

sre-marc: Also applied temporary pod-level limit increase for inference replicas to allow more pods per node (adjusted resource requests to allow binpacking). Command:
```
kubectl set resources deployment inference-worker -n inference --requests=cpu=2,memory=8Gi --limits=cpu=4,memory=16Gi
```

oncall-alex: Heads-up: altering requests may change QoS. We measured that the optimized requests allow 10% more pods per node but slight latency variance.

customer-success-lee: Notifying affected customers: sent out in-product banner and email for known customer orgs. Escalated VIP customers to white-glove channel.

sre-marc: New nodes are starting. Cluster events show nodes registering and kubelet capacity adding GPUs. Pending pods dropping from 42 -> 10.

oncall-alex: Good sign. Monitor p99 and error rates closely. Set short-term alert for error rate > 3%.

infra-bot: Provider autoscaling event: +14 nodes provisioning (type=nv6a). ts=1768002205

sre-marc: After +14 nodes, pending pods now 3, queue length decreasing to +220 requests, p99 latency back to ~320ms for most customers.

devops-julie: Cloud provider confirmed quota increase and nodes are stable. I will follow up with a PR to revert the temporary max nodes change after incident.

oncall-alex: Can we also check for any runaway cron jobs causing burst? I saw a spike at 16:02 UTC from batch-scheduler.

sre-marc: Found a cron burst: nightly-preview-job misconfigured (ran at 16:00 UTC instead of 04:00). Disabled it:
```
kubectl patch cronjob nightly-preview-job -n batch -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'
```

oncall-alex: Nice catch. That explains a portion of the sudden load.

customer-success-lee: Customers reporting service mostly recovered. A few still on degraded performance but we offered temporary credits. Tracking responses.

oncall-alex: Post-incident actions: 1) revert autoscaler max to 80 with controlled rollout and add a slack warning before doing so, 2) update runbook to include immediate routing to secondary region, 3) add alert when autoscaler at >=80% of configured max for 5m, 4) add a deployment guard against cronjobs outside business hours.

devops-julie: I'll file the infra ticket and change the autoscaler PR to include a canary and revert plan. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/compare/PR-4321

sre-marc: Logging summary and timeline in #postmortems once we confirm metrics fully stabilized. I saved relevant logs and kube events.

oncall-alex: Great work team. Marking incident as mitigated, moving to monitoring. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated ts=1768003200 assignees=[oncall-alex,sre-marc,devops-julie]

oncall-alex: Leaving this thread for the next shift. Handoff to night SRE: @sre-night. Key facts in first message.
